plan: 2 Kings 19:1-19; Isaiah 37:1-20; 2 Chronicles 32:9-19; 2 Kings 19:20-37; Isaiah 37:21-38; 2 Chronicles 32:20-23

readings.title: Hezekiah Seeks Counsel from Isaiah
readings.subtitle: In sackcloth and ashes, the king sends his officials to the prophet for a word from YeHoVaH.
readings.text: [2 Kings 19:1] And it came to be, when Sovereign Ḥizqiyahu heard it, that he tore <dn>את</dn> his garments, and covered himself with sackcloth, and went into the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, [2] and sent <dn>את</dn> Elyaqim, who was over the household, and <dn>את</dn> Sheḇnah the scribe, and <dn>את</dn> the elders of the priests, covering themselves with sackcloth, to Yeshayahu the prophet, son of Amots. [3] And they said to him, “Thus said Ḥizqiyahu, ‘This day is a day of distress and rebuke and scorn, for the children have come to birth but there is no power to bring forth. [4] It could be that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> does hear <dn>את</dn> all the words of the Raḇshaqěh, whom his master the sovereign of Ashshur has sent to reproach the living <dn>Elohim</dn>, and shall rebuke <dn>את</dn> the words which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> has heard. Therefore lift up your prayer for the remnant that is left.’ ” [5] And the servants of Sovereign Ḥizqiyahu came to Yeshayahu, [6] and Yeshayahu said to them, “Say this to your master, ‘Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“Do not be afraid of the words which you have heard, with which the servants of the sovereign of Ashshur have reviled <dn>Me</dn>.</dq> [7] <dq>“See, <dn>I</dn> am putting a spirit upon him, and he shall hear a report and return to his own land. And <dn>I</dn> shall cause him to fall by the sword in his land.” ’ ”

readings.title: Sennacherib's Second Threat
readings.subtitle: The king of Assyria sends a letter to Hezekiah, mocking his trust in YeHoVaH.
readings.text: [8] And the Raḇshaqěh returned and found <dn>את</dn> the sovereign of Ashshur fighting against Liḇnah, for he had heard that he had left Laḵish. [9] And when the sovereign heard concerning Tirhaqah sovereign of Kush, “See, he has come out to fight against you,” he again sent messengers to Ḥizqiyahu, saying, [10] “Speak to Ḥizqiyahu sovereign of Yehuḏah, saying, ‘Do not let your <dn>Elohim</dn> in whom you trust deceive you, saying, “Yerushalayim is not given into the hand of the sovereign of Ashshur.” [11] See, you have heard <dn>את</dn> what the sovereigns of Ashshur have done to all lands by putting them under the ban. And are you going to be delivered? [12] Have the mighty ones of the nations delivered those whom my fathers have destroyed: Gozan and Ḥaran and Retseph, and the sons of Ěḏen who were in Telassar? [13] Where is the sovereign of Ḥamath, and the sovereign of Arpaḏ, and the sovereign of the city of Sepharvayim, Hěna, and Ivvah?’ ”

readings.title: Hezekiah's Prayer of Faith
readings.subtitle: Spreading Sennacherib's letter before YeHoVaH, Hezekiah prays for deliverance for the sake of YeHoVaH's name.
readings.text: [14] And Ḥizqiyahu received <dn>את</dn> the letters from the hand of the messengers, and read them, and went up to the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. And Ḥizqiyahu spread it before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [15] And Ḥizqiyahu prayed before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and said, “O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, the One who dwells between the keruḇim, <dn>You</dn> are <dn>Elohim</dn>, <dn>You</dn> alone, of all the reigns of the earth. <dn>You</dn> have made <dn>את</dn> the heavens and <dn>את</dn> earth. [16] “Incline <dn>Your</dn> ear, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and hear. Open <dn>Your</dn> eyes, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and see. And hear <dn>את</dn> the words of Sanḥěriḇ, which he has sent to reproach the living <dn>Elohim</dn>. [17] “Truly, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, the sovereigns of Ashshur have laid waste <dn>את</dn> the nations and their lands, [18] and have put <dn>את</dn> their mighty ones into the fire, for they were not mighty ones, but the work of men’s hands, wood and stone, and destroyed them. [19] “And now, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn>, <dn>I</dn> pray, save us from his hand, so that all the reigns of the earth know that <dn>You</dn> are <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn>, <dn>You</dn> alone.”

readings.title: The King's Distress and the Prophet's Assurance
readings.subtitle: Isaiah records Hezekiah's appeal and YeHoVaH's initial promise of deliverance from the Assyrian threat.
readings.text: [Isaiah 37:1] And it came to be, when Sovereign Ḥizqiyahu heard it, that he tore <dn>את</dn> his clothes, and covered himself with sackcloth, and went into the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, [2] and sent <dn>את</dn> Elyaqim, who was over the household, and <dn>את</dn> Sheḇnah the scribe, and <dn>את</dn> the elders of the priests, covering themselves with sackcloth, to Yeshayahu the prophet, the son of Amots. [3] And they said to him, “Thus said Ḥizqiyahu, ‘This day is a day of distress and rebuke and scorn, for the children have come to birth, but there is no strength to bring forth. [4] It could be that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> does hear <dn>את</dn> the words of the Raḇshaqěh, whom his master the sovereign of Ashshur has sent to reproach the living <dn>Elohim</dn>, and shall rebuke <dn>את</dn> the words which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> has heard. readings.title: The Arrogant Letter from Assyria
readings.subtitle: Sennacherib sends a blasphemous letter, challenging the power of YeHoVaH to deliver Jerusalem.
readings.text: [8] And the Raḇshaqěh returned and found the sovereign of Ashshur fighting against Liḇnah, for he had heard that he had left Laḵish. [9] And he heard concerning Tirhaqah sovereign of Kush, “He has come out to fight with you.” And when he heard it, he sent messengers to Ḥizqiyahu, saying, [10] “Speak to Ḥizqiyahu the sovereign of Yehuḏah, saying, ‘Do not let your <dn>Elohim</dn> in whom you trust deceive you, saying, “Yerushalayim is not given into the hand of the sovereign of Ashshur.” [11] See, you have heard what the sovereigns of Ashshur have done to all lands by putting them under the ban. readings.title: The Prayer Before YeHoVaH
readings.subtitle: Hezekiah presents the Assyrian letter in the Temple, appealing to the Creator of all to vindicate His own Name.
readings.text: [14] And Ḥizqiyahu received <dn>את</dn> the letter from the hand of the messengers, and read it. And Ḥizqiyahu went up to the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and spread it before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [15] And Ḥizqiyahu prayed to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, saying, [16] “O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, the One who dwells between the keruḇim, <dn>You</dn> are <dn>Elohim</dn>, <dn>You</dn> alone, of all the reigns of the earth. <dn>You</dn> have made <dn>את</dn> the heavens and <dn>את</dn> earth. [17] “Incline <dn>Your</dn> ear, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and hear. Open <dn>Your</dn> eyes, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and see. And hear <dn>את</dn> all the words of Sanḥěriḇ, who has sent to reproach the living <dn>Elohim</dn>. [18] “Truly, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, the sovereigns of Ashshur have laid waste <dn>את</dn> all the lands, and their land, [19] and have put <dn>את</dn> their mighty ones into the fire, for they were not mighty ones, but the work of men’s hands, wood and stone. And they destroyed them. [20] “And now, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn>, save us from his hand, so that all the reigns of the earth know that <dn>You</dn> are <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dn>You</dn> alone.”

readings.title: Sennacherib's Psychological Warfare
readings.subtitle: The Assyrian king's servants mock YeHoVaH and Hezekiah's trust, attempting to demoralize the people of Jerusalem.
readings.text: [2 Chronicles 32:9] After this Sanḥěriḇ the sovereign of Ashshur sent <dn>את</dn> his servants to Yerushalayim – but he himself, and all his power with him against Laḵish – to Ḥizqiyahu sovereign of Yehuḏah, and to all Yehuḏah who were in Yerushalayim, saying, [10] “Thus said Sanḥěriḇ the sovereign of Ashshur, ‘On what are you trusting, that you remain in Yerushalayim under siege? [11] Is Ḥizqiyahu not persuading <dn>את</dn> you to give yourselves over to die by scarcity of food and by thirst, saying, “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn> shall deliver us from the hand of the sovereign of Ashshur”? [12] Has not Ḥizqiyahu himself taken away <dn>His</dn> high places and <dn>His</dn> slaughter-places, and ordered Yehuḏah and Yerushalayim, saying, “Bow yourselves before one slaughter-place and burn incense on it”? [13] Do you not know <dn>את</dn> what <dn>I</dn> and my fathers have done to all the peoples of other lands? Were the mighty ones of the nations of those lands in any way able to deliver their lands out of my hand? [14] Who was there among all the mighty ones of those nations that my fathers put under the ban that could deliver <dn>את</dn> his people from my hand, that your <dn>Elohim</dn> should be able to deliver you from my hand? [15] And now, do not let Ḥizqiyahu deceive <dn>את</dn> you or persuade <dn>את</dn> you like this, and do not believe him; for no mighty one of any nation or reign was able to deliver his people from my hand or the hand of my fathers – much less your <dn>Elohim</dn>, to deliver you from my hand!’ ” [16] And his servants spoke even more against <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> and against <dn>His</dn> servant Ḥizqiyahu. [17] And he wrote letters to reproach <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, and to speak against <dn>Him</dn>, saying, “As the mighty ones of the nations of other lands have not delivered their people from my hand, so the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Ḥizqiyahu shall not deliver <dn>His</dn> people from my hand.” [18] Then they called out with a loud voice in the language of Yehuḏah to the people of Yerushalayim who were on the wall, to frighten them and to trouble them, in order to capture the city. [19] And they spoke against the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yerushalayim, as against the mighty ones of the people of the earth, the work of men’s hands.

readings.title: The Rebuke of Sennacherib's Pride
readings.subtitle: Through Isaiah, YeHoVaH addresses the arrogance of the Assyrian king, declaring his fate.
readings.text: [2 Kings 19:20] Then Yeshayahu son of Amots sent to Ḥizqiyahu, saying, “Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, <dq>‘<dn>I</dn> have heard <dn>את</dn> that which you have prayed to <dn>Me</dn> against Sanḥěriḇ sovereign of Ashshur.’</dq> [21] <dq>“This is the word which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has spoken concerning him, ‘The maiden, the daughter of Tsiyon, has despised you, mocked you; the daughter of Yerushalayim has shaken her head behind you!</dq> [22] <dq>Whom have you reproached and reviled? Against whom have you raised a voice, and lifted up your eyes on high? Against the Set-apart One of Yisra’ěl!</dq> [23] <dq>By the hand of your messengers you have reproached <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and said, “With my many chariots <dn>I</dn> have come up to the height of the mountains, to the sides of Leḇanon. And <dn>I</dn> cut down its tall cedars, its choice cypress trees. And <dn>I</dn> enter its remotest parts, its thickest forest.</dq> [24] <dq><dn>I</dn> have dug and drunk strange water, and with the soles of my feet <dn>I</dn> dry up all the streams of defence.”</dq> [25] <dq>Have you not heard long ago, <dn>I</dn> made <dn>את</dn> it; from days of old <dn>I</dn> formed it? Now <dn>I</dn> have brought it to be, that you should make walled cities ruinous heaps.</dq> [26] <dq>And their inhabitants were powerless, they were overthrown and put to shame, they were as the grass of the field and the green plants, as the grass on the house-tops and withered before it came up.</dq> [27] <dq>But <dn>I</dn> know your sitting down, and your going out and your coming in, and your rage against <dn>Me</dn>.</dq> [28] <dq>Because your rage against <dn>Me</dn> and your pride have come up to <dn>My</dn> ears, <dn>I</dn> shall put <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> hook in your nose and <dn>My</dn> bridle in your lips, and <dn>I</dn> shall turn you back by the way which you came.</dq>

readings.title: The Sign and Promise of Deliverance
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH gives a sign of agricultural restoration and promises that the remnant of Judah will be preserved.
readings.text: [29] <dq>And this is <dn>את</dn> the sign for you: This year you eat what grows of itself, and in the second year what springs from that, and in the third year sow and reap and plant vineyards and eat their fruit.</dq> [30] <dq>And the remnant who have escaped of the house of Yehuḏah shall again take root downward, and be fruitful.</dq> [31] <dq>For out of Yerushalayim comes forth a remnant, and those who escape from Mount Tsiyon – the ardour of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> does <dn>את</dn> this.’</dq> [32] <dq>“Therefore thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> concerning the sovereign of Ashshur, ‘<dn>He</dn> does not come into this city, nor does he shoot an arrow there, nor does he come before it with shield, nor does he build a siege mound against it.</dq> [33] <dq>By the way that he came, by the same he turns back. And he does not come into this city,’ declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [34] <dq>And <dn>I</dn> shall defend this city, to save it for <dn>My</dn> own sake and for the sake of Daviḏ <dn>My</dn> servant.’ ”

readings.title: The Angelic Strike and Sennacherib's Demise
readings.subtitle: The messenger of YeHoVaH decimates the Assyrian camp, and Sennacherib is assassinated by his own sons.
readings.text: [35] And it came to be in that night that the messenger of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> went out, and struck in the camp of Ashshur one hundred and eighty-five thousand. And they rose up early in the morning and saw all of them dead bodies. [36] And Sanḥěriḇ sovereign of Ashshur broke camp and went away, and turned back, and remained in Ninevěh. [37] And it came to be, as he was bowing himself in the house of Nisroḵ his mighty one, that his sons Aḏrammeleḵ and Shar‘etser struck him with the sword, and they escaped into the land of Ararat. And his son Ěsarḥaddon reigned in his place.

readings.title: The Word Against the King of Assyria
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH responds to Hezekiah's prayer with a powerful prophecy against the prideful Sennacherib.
readings.text: [Isaiah 37:21] Then Yeshayahu son of Amots sent to Ḥizqiyahu, saying, “Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, <dq>‘Because you have prayed to <dn>Me</dn> against Sanḥěriḇ sovereign of Ashshur,</dq> [22] <dq>this is the word which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has spoken concerning him, “The maiden, the daughter of Tsiyon, has despised you, mocked you; the daughter of Yerushalayim has shaken her head behind you!</dq> [23] <dq>“Whom have you reproached and reviled? And against whom have you raised your voice, and lifted up your eyes in pride? Against the Set-apart One of Yisra’ěl!</dq> [24] <dq>“By the hand of your servants you have reproached <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and said, ‘With my many chariots <dn>I</dn> have come up to the height of the mountains, to the limits of Leḇanon. And <dn>I</dn> cut down its tall cedars and its choice cypress trees. And <dn>I</dn> enter its farthest height, its thickest forest.</dq> [25] <dq><dn>I</dn> have dug and drunk water, and with the soles of my feet <dn>I</dn> have dried up all the streams of defence.’</dq> [26] <dq>“Have you not heard long ago how <dn>I</dn> made <dn>את</dn> it, from days of old, that <dn>I</dn> formed it? Now <dn>I</dn> have brought it about, that you should be for crushing walled cities into heaps of ruins.</dq> [27] <dq>“And their inhabitants were powerless, they were overthrown and put to shame. They were as the grass of the field and as the green plant, as the grass on the house-tops and as grain blighted before it is grown.</dq> [28] <dq>“But <dn>I</dn> know your sitting down, and your going out and your coming in, and your rage against <dn>Me</dn>.</dq> [29] <dq>“Because your rage against <dn>Me</dn> and your pride have come up to <dn>My</dn> ears, <dn>I</dn> shall put <dn>My</dn> hook in your nose and <dn>My</dn> bridle in your lips, and <dn>I</dn> shall turn you back by the way which you came.</dq>

readings.title: A Sign for Judah and a Promise of Defense
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH promises to defend Jerusalem for His own sake and for David's, giving a sign of future prosperity.
readings.text: [30] <dq>“And this shall be <dn>את</dn> the sign for you: This year you eat such as grows of itself, and the second year what springs from that, and in the third year sow and reap, plant vineyards, and eat the fruit of them.</dq> [31] <dq>“And the remnant who have escaped of the house of Yehuḏah shall again take root downward, and be fruitful upward.</dq> [32] <dq>“For out of Yerushalayim comes forth a remnant, and those who escape from Mount Tsiyon – the ardour of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts does <dn>את</dn> this.</dq> [33] <dq>“Therefore thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> concerning the sovereign of Ashshur, ‘<dn>He</dn> does not come into this city, nor does he shoot an arrow there, nor does he come before it with shield, nor does he build a siege mound against it.</dq> [34] <dq>By the way that he came, by the same he turns back. And into this city he does not come,’ declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [35] <dq>And <dn>I</dn> shall defend this city, to save it for <dn>My</dn> own sake and for the sake of <dn>My</dn> servant Daviḏ.’ ”

readings.title: The Fall of the Assyrian Army and its King
readings.subtitle: Isaiah records the fulfillment of the prophecy: the destruction of Sennacherib's army and his assassination in Nineveh.
readings.text: [36] And a messenger of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> went out, and struck in the camp of Ashshur one hundred and eighty-five thousand. And they arose early in the morning, and saw all of them, dead bodies. [37] And Sanḥěriḇ the sovereign of Ashshur broke camp and went away, and turned back, and remained at Ninevěh. [38] And it came to be, as he was bowing himself in the house of Nisroḵ his mighty one, that his sons Aḏrammeleḵ and Shar’etser struck him with the sword, and they escaped into the land of Ararat. And his son Ěsarḥaddon reigned in his place.

readings.title: Divine Intervention and National Exaltation
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH saves Jerusalem, and Hezekiah is honored by all nations as a result of the miraculous deliverance.
readings.text: [2 Chronicles 32:20] And Sovereign Ḥizqiyahu and the prophet Yeshayahu, son of Amots, prayed about this, and cried out to the heavens. [21] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> sent a messenger who cut down <dn>את</dn> every mighty brave one, both the leader and the commander in the camp of the sovereign of Ashshur, and he returned shamefaced to his own land, and went into the house of his mighty one, and there some of his own offspring caused him to fall by the sword. [22] Thus <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> saved <dn>את</dn> Ḥizqiyahu and <dn>את</dn> the inhabitants of Yerushalayim from the hand of Sanḥěriḇ the sovereign of Ashshur, and from the hand of all others, and guided them on every side. [23] And many brought gifts to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> at Yerushalayim, and presents to Ḥizqiyahu sovereign of Yehuḏah, and he was exalted in the eyes of all nations thereafter.
